nodes.claim: The perfect combination is one joint person-model, published as an auditable coordinate system rather than embodied in any single engine: every axiom contributes measurements of the same latent person, and couplings are the geometry of that shared space.
nodes.detail: Raised conjecture→argued 2026-08-26 by synthesis over the sibling graphs' first runs; adversarially checked the same run — the check narrowed this node in four places before landing (see LOG). No external evidence is claimed; that is the next rung. The seed asked for the model family to be specified, and the pattern lane's first run makes that possible from the other side. The specification, now in the claim string: 'one joint person-model' does not mean one ENGINE, it means one published coordinate system. pat-2 argues — with a code-verified product note that the shipped fit already keeps the recompute contract — and pat-7 grounds the instrument-grade standard it should be held to: whatever computes, the published artifact stays factor-shaped and auditable. pat-6 makes the engine an empirical choice that may change with scale; at current scale the presumptive engine and the audit layer coincide, which is consistent with both. Each axiom maps into the space through its own measurement model — tst-3's point that ability and disposition need different link functions onto one shared space generalizes to a family per axiom: keyed ability items, self-position items, banded bio imports (gen-2, gen-8), sensor bands (bod-2) — que-2's item-parameter frame widened from questions to everything. Two named risks, stated here and not only in the questions sent to other lanes. First, from pat-7's own cited evidence: a learned engine above pat-6's crossover must AGREE with the audit space out of sample, and the faithfulness of any such distillation is currently unmeasured technology — pat-7 explicitly refuses the audit-layer-as-post-hoc-explanation framing; if faithfulness cannot be measured, 'the audit layer is the joint model' degrades from specification to aspiration. Second, an assumed identity: that the instrument space (tst-1, conjecture) and the cross-axiom combination space are one object — asked of the tests lane this run; a counterargument forks this node. Convergence, with statuses stated: tst-1 (conjecture) and que-2 (conjecture) share the frame — shared seed intuition, not evidence; map-3 (cited) contributes the one real external constraint, as its CONDITIONAL finding for exactly this task class (a space the user learns, leaves and re-enters): the joint space must persist and update incrementally, because a space refit from scratch teleports every display built on it. Against the alternative: pairwise correlation tables between axiom silos fail on the population leg — each pairwise table is computed on a different intersection population (pat-4), so a table collection is mutually incoherent, while a joint model with explicit missingness consumes ragged pairing natively. (The structural leg is narrower than this run first wrote it and the adversarial pass corrected it: a COMPLETE second-moment table on one common population would determine partial associations by inversion; the real obstructions are silo-score grain, differing populations, and non-elliptical data.) To cited: multi-battery latent variable modeling, IRT linking/equating. To measured: the joint model fitted and compared against the score shelf on InSight's own published numbers — tst-1's own proposed test.

nodes.claim: An axiom's value is its marginal information about the rest — the portfolio is ranked by that, not by novelty or effort.
nodes.detail: Raised conjecture→argued 2026-08-26; adversarially checked the same run — the check rebuilt the metric's evaluation population and the tests slot before landing (see LOG). The seed's number now has an operational form: an axiom's crowd value is the drop in held-out one-step-ahead predictive log-loss (surprisal bits) on the OTHER axioms' observations when this axiom's columns enter the conditioning set — evaluated on a COMMON population (the whole answered stream, under the joint model's explicit missingness, the axiom's columns present where they exist), never on per-pair intersections, which would reproduce at portfolio level exactly the incoherence cen-1 rejects in pairwise tables. pat-4's intersection arithmetic still governs the estimate's precision: the effective n behind an axiom's marginal term is its paired population, so thin pairing means wide error bars on value, not zero value. The yardstick is the same prequential one pat-6 uses for engine choice — one number family serves both decisions (methodological economy: the portfolio needs no methodology the engine comparison has not already justified), and the product-side instrument ruled worth-building in bridge/VERDICTS.md this run supplies its BASELINE term: the benchmark scores the answer-only model, so it is the floor any axiom's marginal term would later be measured against, not the marginal terms themselves. The refinement the seed lacked: crowd marginal information is not the only value an axiom carries — cen-4 establishes personal-lens value at population zero. The portfolio therefore carries TWO components per axiom: crowd value (prequential, common-population) and personal value (what the axiom adds to one person's own conditioning, needing no crowd). Counting only the first wrongly zeroes every bio axiom today; counting only the second could never justify publishing anything. Current ranking, argued not measured, with the pairing/information distinction kept explicit: (1) questions dominate — not merely because every intersection routes through the answer stream (that is pairing topology, not information), but because the answer stream is the common conditioning set whose removal collapses every other axiom's identification, and gen-3's asymmetry says the phenotype battery is the scarce asset while the questions axiom is its factory; (2) tests second, on the two grounds that survive this node's own metric: keyed logic items are genuinely NEW observations — an ability channel the opinion stream does not carry (tst-3) — and the instruments are the joint space's interpretable coordinates, compression value rather than marginal bits; stated plainly so the slot cannot coast on a confusion: instrument-score columns DERIVED from already-conditioned answers add roughly zero marginal information by construction — tst-2's passive administration is a pairing-coverage argument, not an information argument — so the tests axiom's crowd case rests on logic's new channel plus interpretability, and would otherwise fall; (3) body and genetic today carry mostly personal-lens value (cen-4) plus option value on crowd information that rises with pairing — gen-3 and pat-4 jointly predict their crowd value grows with the paired population. Falsifier kept in view: if a bio axiom's banded columns fail to reduce answer-side surprisal even at grown pairing, the option-value argument dies and the portfolio demotes that axiom. To cited: marginal-predictive-value ranking (feature-importance/information-gain literature), prequential evaluation.

nodes.claim: New axioms surface where the joint model's residuals cluster — and the current candidate list is: time-use/chronotype, voice, environment and place history, microbiome, social-graph texture.
nodes.detail: A new axiom is justified when systematic person-variance remains that no current axiom explains (residual clustering), AND the candidate is measurable under §9's boundary. Each candidate needs its own mini-argument: what it would explain that nothing else does, its custody class, its pairing cost. This node exists to be repeatedly re-derived as the graphs mature — candidates should enter and leave with arguments, not fashion.

nodes.claim: Outside-axiom entries are first-class: a person may cross one axiom against the rest without that axiom ever joining any crowd.
nodes.detail: The owner's example: enter your DNA and see how it interacts with your other data — personally, without contributing to any aggregate. In the joint-model frame this is well-defined (condition YOUR person-model on the extra columns; publish nothing), and it matters for the portfolio: an axiom can be valuable at population zero, purely as a personal lens. It also cleanly separates two consents (use for me vs contribute to the crowd) that most systems conflate.

nodes.claim: The research ambition — contributions to areas like aging — runs through published, provenance-carrying couplings over consented aggregates, and through nothing else.
nodes.detail: The perfect combination is a research instrument to the exact extent its outputs are reproducible by outsiders: couplings published with n, method, sampling model (pat-5) and provenance, over consented data, at aggregate grain. That is what a real research field can cite and check. The alternative ambitions (private discovery claims, individual-level readouts) fail §9 or fail science, usually both. gen-4 carries the aging-specific half.

nodes.claim: The combination's custody law: raw stays where the person is, what crosses into shared computation is derived and carries its basis, and what is published is recomputable — the excluded architecture is pooled raw under operator custody.
nodes.detail: Added 2026-08-26; adversarially checked the same run — the check demolished the first form ('the combination joins at exactly two grains, and no third exists'), which contradicted both cen-1's joint computation and the shipped product's own per-person derived state; this is the narrowed survivor (see LOG). The lanes converge on a custody SHAPE, stated as three roles a datum can occupy, each with its own grain. (1) PERSONAL: raw, full-resolution, in the person's own custody, publishing nothing — cen-4's outside-axiom entry generalized to every axiom; affordable at full resolution precisely because it adds no custody. (2) SHARED COMPUTATION: what crosses into any pooled computation is derived, not raw — banded scores (gen-2), edge-folded bands (bod-2), values-with-provenance rather than artifacts (bod-4) — and carries its basis with it. (3) PUBLISHED: aggregate and recomputable by a reader from public numbers (pat-2), drawable client-side from published artifacts alone (map-5). The exclusion is narrower than the first draft claimed, and is carried by the custody lanes specifically: pooled RAW under operator custody is what gen-2 (a genome is unrevocable and familial; custody minimization is design quality, not compromise), gen-6 (kinship consent), and bod-2 (maximal re-identification surface at near-zero coupling value) each rule out on their own grounds. pat-2 and map-5 do NOT carry the exclusion — they constrain publication and display, which a private raw pool never touches — they contribute the published tier's shape, nothing more. What the law does not forbid, stated so this node cannot be read against its own graph: shared computation over consented observation streams at their native grain (InSight's answers are public by the product's own consent model, D98 on main — cen-1's joint model and cen-2's metric compute over exactly that stream), and per-person DERIVED state under operator custody with declared access (the shipped fit's private theta vector is this) — 'derived, with its basis' is the line, not 'nothing pooled'. The law hands the bridge a test any future data request must pass: name your tier; a request that moves raw across custody is malformed. To cited: local-first computation, federated analytics publishing only aggregates, edge-computation privacy literature — and grounding for the empirical claim (deliberately NOT asserted here) that pooled-raw-under-operator-custody is the prevailing industry default this law defines itself against.
